title: Depth-Alarm Grounding Guard
dataSources: NMEA/SignalK data (`nmea:reading`), bilge pump (`bilge:event`), mooring/anchor watch (`mooring:status`), marine weather (`marineweather:forecast`).
app: Marine electronics — NMEA 2000 / SignalK boat networks, bilge, battery and shore-power sensors, anchor-watch GPS, and marine weather feeds — streamed to Splunk HEC via SignalK and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=nmea:reading measurement=depth
| where depth_m<safety_depth_m
| stats min(depth_m) as shallowest, count as alerts by _time
| sort - _time
description: Alerts whenever the water depth falls below your safety margin, guarding against running aground.
value: Shallow water appears fast; a depth alarm gives the seconds needed to turn away before grounding.
implementation: Ingest depth-sounder data into `index=personal`; alert when depth drops below a safety threshold.
visualization: Time chart of depth with grounding-alarm markers.
grandmaExplanation: It warns the moment the water gets too shallow, helping you avoid running the boat aground.
